title: Klopp appointed Liverpool manager
summary: Four days after Brendan Rodgers was sacked, Liverpool appointed Jürgen Klopp. In his first club interview he asked supporters to change from doubter to believer; at the Anfield press conference next morning he called himself the Normal One.

title: Late equaliser, then the salute to the Kop
summary: Divock Origi equalised deep into stoppage time. Klopp then led his players towards the Kop, arms linked. Some rivals mocked it; he later said he wanted to thank the supporters and show that players and crowd were one unit.

title: The Dortmund comeback at Anfield
summary: Dortmund led 3–1 on the night after 57 minutes. Coutinho and Sakho scored, and Dejan Lovren headed the winner in the first minute of stoppage time, 4–3 on the night and 5–4 on aggregate, against Klopp's old club.

title: Europa League final lost in Basel
summary: Daniel Sturridge put Liverpool ahead before half-time, but Sevilla equalised straight after half-time and won 3–1. Klopp said his team had lost faith in their style of play. It was his second lost final in three months.

title: Summer 2016 signings: Mané, Matip, Wijnaldum
summary: Sadio Mané arrived from Southampton on 28 June and Georginio Wijnaldum from Newcastle United. Joël Matip, agreed in February, joined from Schalke on a free transfer. Contemporary estimates had Liverpool selling more than they bought that summer.

title: Sadio Mané signs from Southampton
summary: Liverpool completed the signing of Mané from Southampton on 28 June.

title: Joël Matip joins on a free transfer
summary: Matip's move from Schalke was confirmed in February and he joined on 1 July.

title: Georginio Wijnaldum signs from Newcastle
summary: Wijnaldum joined from Newcastle United, who had just been relegated, on a five-year contract.

title: Fourth place secured on the final day
summary: Goals from Wijnaldum, Coutinho and Lallana beat already relegated Middlesbrough and secured fourth place on 76 points. That earned a Champions League play-off in August, not a place in the group stage.

title: Summer 2017 signings: Salah and Robertson
summary: Liverpool announced Mohamed Salah from Roma on 22 June, effective 1 July. Andrew Robertson joined from relegated Hull City. Robertson took the left-back place in December, and Salah scored 44 goals in all competitions that season.

title: Mohamed Salah joins from Roma
summary: Liverpool announced Salah's signing on Thursday 22 June, effective from 1 July, on a five-year contract.

title: Andrew Robertson joins from Hull City
summary: Robertson arrived from Hull, who had just been relegated, and became first-choice left-back after Alberto Moreno's ankle injury in December.

title: Van Dijk arrives; Coutinho leaves
summary: Liverpool agreed to sign Virgil van Dijk on 27 December and registered him from 1 January. He scored the winner on his FA Cup debut on 5 January. The next day Philippe Coutinho agreed a move to Barcelona, completed on 8 January.

title: Virgil van Dijk joins from Southampton
summary: The deal was agreed on 27 December 2017 and Van Dijk was registered from 1 January, in time for the Champions League knockout stage.

title: Philippe Coutinho leaves for Barcelona
summary: Klopp said Coutinho had made clear that the move to Barcelona was his dream and that nothing was left to change his mind.

title: Liverpool 4–3 Manchester City
summary: City had not lost a league game all season. Oxlade-Chamberlain, Firmino, Mané and Salah scored for Liverpool, the first side to beat City in the league. Klopp said it showed it was possible to play without Coutinho.

title: City beaten in the Champions League
summary: Salah, Oxlade-Chamberlain and Mané scored inside 31 minutes in the first leg at Anfield. In Manchester, Salah and Firmino scored in a 2–1 win, so Liverpool won the quarter-final 5–1 on aggregate.

title: First leg at Anfield
summary: Three goals in the first 31 minutes put Liverpool in command.

title: Second leg at the Etihad
summary: City scored after two minutes, then Salah and Firmino turned the match around.

title: Champions League final lost in Kyiv
summary: Salah went off injured after about half an hour. Loris Karius made two errors and Gareth Bale scored twice after coming on, so Real Madrid won 3–1. A hospital later concluded Karius had suffered a concussion in the match.

title: Summer 2018 signings: Alisson and Fabinho
summary: Fabinho was announced on 28 May, two days after Kyiv, and joined from Monaco on 1 July. Alisson Becker signed from Roma on 19 July. Klopp later said Liverpool had chosen to become stronger defensively.

title: Fabinho joins from Monaco
summary: Liverpool announced Fabinho's signing on 28 May, with the defensive midfielder joining on 1 July.

title: Alisson Becker signs from Roma
summary: Alisson signed from Roma on 19 July, and Loris Karius left on loan to Beşiktaş on 25 August.

title: Liverpool 4–0 Barcelona
summary: Trailing 3–0 from the first leg, and without Salah and Firmino, Liverpool won 4–0. Origi scored twice, Wijnaldum twice in just over two minutes, and Alexander-Arnold's quickly taken corner led to the fourth goal.

title: 97 points, one short
summary: Mané scored twice to beat Wolves, but Manchester City won 4–1 at Brighton and took the title with 98 points to Liverpool's 97. Liverpool lost only one league match all season, at the Etihad on 3 January.

title: Champions of Europe in Madrid
summary: Salah scored from a penalty inside two minutes and Origi added a second in the 87th. It was Liverpool's sixth European Cup and Klopp's first trophy with the club, ending a run of six major cup-final defeats.

title: World champions: the Club World Cup final
summary: Mané set up Firmino for the only goal in the 99th minute, and Liverpool won the Club World Cup for the first time. With the first team in Qatar, a young side had lost 5–0 at Aston Villa in the League Cup.

title: Champions of England after 30 years
summary: Chelsea's 2–1 win over Manchester City on 25 June confirmed the title with seven games left. The season had been suspended on 13 March and restarted behind closed doors; the trophy was lifted before an empty Kop on 22 July.

title: The season stops, then restarts
summary: The Premier League suspended its season on 13 March, and Liverpool's first match back was on 21 June, behind closed doors.

title: The trophy lifted on an empty Kop
summary: After a 5–3 win over Chelsea, Kenny Dalglish handed the trophy to Jordan Henderson, who lifted it on a stage built on the Kop.
